'''Lassana "Lass" Diarra''' (born 10 March 1985) is a French former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defensive midfielder]].

Diarra spent his club career at [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], in addition to two Russian outfits – [[FC Anzhi Makhachkala|Anzhi Makhachkala]] and [[FC Lokomotiv Moscow|Lokomotiv Moscow]], before retiring in 2019. He was also a [[France national football team|French international]] with 34 caps between 2007 and 2016.

==Early life==
Born in [[Paris]] to Malian parents,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2756920-after-travails-and-tragedy-lassana-diarra-faces-real-madrid-reunion-with-psg | title=After Travails and Tragedy, Lassana Diarra Faces Real Madrid Reunion with PSG | website=[[Bleacher Report]] }}</ref> Diarra began playing football at the sports center on Rue Julien-Lacroix in [[Belleville, Paris|Belleville]], the district in which he grew up in the [[20th arrondissement of Paris]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Les people de Belleville : Lassana Diarra {{!}} Belleville Belleville |url=http://www.belleville-belleville.com/les-people-de-belleville-lassana-diarra/ |access-date=30 May 2021 |work=Belleville-Belleville |language=fr}}</ref> After having started his youth club career at [[Paris FC]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Le FC Nantes rétribué pour avoir formé Lassana Diarra |url=https://www.20minutes.fr/sport/64748-20051116-sport-le-fc-nantes-retribue-pour-avoir-forme-lassana-diarra |work=20minutes |date=16 November 2005 |archive-url=http://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/20151128054744/http://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=https://www.20minutes.fr/sport/64748-20051116-sport-le-fc-nantes-retribue-pour-avoir-forme-lassana-diarra |archive-date=28 November 2015 |language=fr}}</ref> Diarra was turned down by multiple football clubs as a youngster; [[FC Nantes|Nantes]] deemed him too "small and lightweight" to succeed at 170&nbsp;cm and 58&nbsp;kg (5'7" and 9 [[Stone (unit)|stone]]).<ref name="AS">{{cite web|url=https://futbol.as.com/futbol/2010/01/02/mas_futbol/1262417229_850215.html|publisher=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|access-date=4 February 2014|author=C. Colino|title=Xabi saca el balón y yo hago más la guerra|date=2 January 2010 }}</ref> He admitted he thought his "football career was over."<ref name="AS"/> His next stop was [[Le Mans Union Club 72|Le Mans UC]], where Diarra claimed they "didn't seem to care" about him.<ref name="AS"/> He would also play shortly for [[FC Red Star Saint-Ouen|Red Star 93]] from the Paris-suburb of [[Saint-Ouen-sur-Seine]].<ref>{{cite news |title=The football club founded by Jules Rimet battles its way back |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-36195987 |work=BBC News |date=3 May 2016 |quote=Newcastle United's Moussa Sissoko, Lassana Diarra, formerly of Chelsea, Arsenal, Real Madrid and Portsmouth and ex-Arsenal player Abou Diaby went through Red Star's youth scheme}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Le Havre===
Diarra's footballing career began at [[Le Havre AC|Le Havre]], a former French top-flight football team. Outstanding in his defensive midfield role, his reputation started to grow and impressive performances saw his selection to the French under-21 squad. Along with the reputation came interest from other clubs, and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] became potential suitors. With Chelsea's [[Claude Makélélé]] getting older, Chelsea's scouts tagged Diarra as the "new Makélélé". Diarra was spotted by [[Gwyn Williams (football manager)|Gwyn Williams]]<ref name="Talentspotter">{{cite web|title=Lassana Diarra: Talentspotter|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/lassana-diarra-talentspotter|website=FourFourTwo|access-date=16 June 2017|date=1 February 2006}}</ref> playing for France in the 2005 [[Toulon Tournament]] and initially came on trial, before the club paid £1&nbsp;million for his services in July 2005.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1103886 |title=DIARRA MOVES TO ARSENAL &#124; News Article &#124; News &#124; Official Site &#124; Chelsea Football Club |website=www.chelseafc.com |access-date=2 February 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140204234442/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1103886 |archive-date=4 February 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Chelsea===
[[File:Lassana Diarra.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Diarra during his time at [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].]]
Diarra was in Chelsea's first team squad in the [[2005–06 Chelsea F.C. season|2005–06 season]], but did not see much first-team football. His Chelsea debut came in the [[UEFA Champions League]] in October 2005, when he was given a brief run out as a substitute when Chelsea were 4–0 up against [[Real Betis]]. Learning from Claude Makélélé he played well against [[Huddersfield Town F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] in the [[FA Cup]] third round, winning rave reviews from both managers, teammates, and media sources. He made his league debut when he came on as a substitute for Makélélé on 5 February 2006 in a 2–0 win over [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Chelsea 2-0 Liverpool|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4657240.stm|publisher=BBC|access-date=27 October 2015|date=5 February 2006}}</ref> He became a bit part player in Chelsea's first team and also completed the full 90 minutes in Chelsea's last two games of the season at [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] and [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] respectively, as manager [[José Mourinho]] rotated his squad. This meant Diarra ended the season with three league appearances as Chelsea won the [[2005–06 FA Premier League]]. Diarra was named Chelsea's Young Player of the Season for 2005–06.<ref name="ars1">{{cite web|title=Arsenal sign Lassana Diarra from Chelsea|url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/arsenal-sign-lassana-diarra-from-chelsea|publisher=Arsenal.com|access-date=3 November 2014|date=31 August 2007|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141103212754/http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/arsenal-sign-lassana-diarra-from-chelsea|archive-date=3 November 2014}}</ref>

Due to Chelsea's defensive injury setbacks during the [[2006–07 Chelsea F.C. season|2006–07 season]], he was often asked to play at right back. He played full Premier League games against Blackburn, [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] and [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]], with some success. He also started in Chelsea's win over [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the [[2007 Football League Cup Final|League Cup Final]] at the [[Millennium Stadium]].<ref name="ars1" /> He was an unused substitute as Chelsea won the [[2007 FA Cup Final]] against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. On 29 July, reports surfaced suggesting he could be on his way to Arsenal in pursuit of first-team football.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11670/2632426/gunners-line-up-diarra-deal |title=Gunners line up Diarra deal &#124; Football News |work=Sky Sports |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> Despite this, he came on as a substitute for Chelsea in the [[2007 FA Community Shield]]. His contract with Chelsea was due to expire in January 2008, and having made no move to extend it, Chelsea sold him to Arsenal on 31 August 2007, before he could leave on a [[free transfer (association football)|free transfer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/-/Actualites/-/600000000000000000000000004578 |title=L'Equipe – Arsenal piste Lassana Diarra |work=L'Équipe |location=France |date=31 July 2007 |access-date=4 February 2014}}</ref>

===Arsenal===
[[File:LassanaDiarra.JPG|thumb|left|150px|Diarra training during his time at [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].]]

On 31 August 2007, transfer deadline day, he signed for Arsenal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>[http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/wenger-all-of-them-can-play-in-the-first-team]{{dead link|date=July 2016}}</ref> He was given the number 8 shirt, vacated by the departure of winger [[Freddie Ljungberg]]. On his move across [[London]], he cited Gunners manager [[Arsène Wenger]] as one of the main reasons for joining the club, along with the style of football played by Arsenal. Wenger had called the young Frenchman a "multi-functional player", and a good addition to the squad.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal sign Lassana Diarra from Chelsea |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/arsenal-sign-lassana-diarra-from-chelsea |publisher=Arsenal.com |date=31 August 2007 |access-date=5 February 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222070819/http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/arsenal-sign-lassana-diarra-from-chelsea |archive-date=22 February 2014}}</ref> Diarra made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute in the home leg of the [[2007–08 UEFA Champions League|2007–08 Champions League]] group stage match against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], and his full debut against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in the third round of the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]]. He then started his first Premier League match for Arsenal against [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on 24 November 2007.<ref>{{cite news|title=Arsenal 2-0 Wigan|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7099687.stm|publisher=BBC|access-date=27 October 2015|date=24 November 2007}}</ref> With the emergence of defensive midfielder [[Mathieu Flamini]] in the Arsenal side, Diarra saw only limited action in the early months of the season. Having expressed concerns that he was not playing enough first team football,<ref>{{cite news |title=Lassana Diarra: I want to leave Arsenal |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2328660/Lassana-Diarra-I-want-to-leave-Arsenal.html |work=The Telegraph|date=6 December 2007 |access-date=5 February 2014 | location=London | first1=Charlie | last1=Caroe}}</ref> Diarra signed for [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] in January 2008 after only five months at Arsenal for an undisclosed fee believed to be around £5.5&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arsenal.com/article.asp?article=486459&lid=NewsHeadline&sub=French+midfielder+leaves+Arsenal+for+the+south+coast&sublid=NewsHeadline&Title=French+midfielder+leaves+Arsenal+for+the+south+coast&f=rss|title=French midfielder leaves Arsenal for the south coast |access-date=17 January 2008 |date=17 January 2008 |publisher=Arsenal.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080118125735/http://www.arsenal.com/article.asp?article=486459&lid=NewsHeadline&sub=French%2Bmidfielder%2Bleaves%2BArsenal%2Bfor%2Bthe%2Bsouth%2Bcoast&sublid=NewsHeadline&Title=French%2Bmidfielder%2Bleaves%2BArsenal%2Bfor%2Bthe%2Bsouth%2Bcoast&f=rss|archive-date=18 January 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Portsmouth===
Diarra signed for Portsmouth on 17 January 2008.<ref>{{cite news |title=Diarra agrees Pompey deal |url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11674/3052445/ |publisher=Sky Sports |date=17 January 2008 |access-date=5 February 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Backtracking Diarra commits to Portsmouth |url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/premier_league/portsmouth/article3212821.ece |work=The Times |location=UK |date=18 January 2008 |access-date=9 June 2008 }}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He was given his first start against [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Portsmouth 3–1 Derby Match Report |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7184823.stm |publisher=BBC |date=19 January 2008 |access-date=9 June 2008 |first=Chris |last=Whyatt}}</ref> contributing to a 3–1 win at [[Fratton Park]]. He scored his first goal for the club in the following match, against [[FA Cup]] Fourth Round [[Football League Championship|Championship]] opponents [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Portsmouth 2–1 Plymouth Match Report |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/7197718.stm |publisher=BBC |date=26 January 2008 |access-date=9 June 2008 |first=Sarah |last=Holt}}</ref> and his first Premier League goal two weeks later, a controversial late winner against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Bolton 0–1 Portsmouth Match Report |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7223964.stm |publisher=BBC |date=9 February 2008 |access-date=9 June 2008 |first=Jamie |last=Lillywhite}}</ref> Diarra went on to play in every minute of Portsmouth's remaining [[2007–08 FA Cup|FA Cup]] matches en route to claiming the trophy in the [[2008 FA Cup Final|final]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Preston 0–1 Portsmouth Match Report |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/7224068.stm |publisher=BBC |date=17 February 2008 |access-date=9 June 2008 |first=Aimee |last=Lewis}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Man Utd 0–1 Portsmouth Match Report |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/7272806.stm |publisher=BBC |date=8 March 2008 |access-date=9 June 2008 |first=Phil |last=McNulty}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=West Brom 0–1 Portsmouth Match Report |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/7320356.stm |publisher=BBC |date=5 April 2008 |access-date=9 June 2008 |first=Andrew |last=McKenzie}}</ref><ref name="cup08">{{cite news |title=Portsmouth 1–0 Cardiff Match Report |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/fa_cup/7393770.stm |publisher=BBC |date=17 May 2008 |access-date=9 June 2008 |first=Phil |last=McNulty}}</ref> He topped the [[2007–08 Premier League|season]] by being included in the [[France national football team|France]] squad for [[UEFA Euro 2008]]; this and the FA Cup win arguably vindicated his decision to part company with Arsenal, Diarra himself saying that it had "more than justified my decision."<ref name="France leave out Cisse & Flamini">{{cite news |title=France leave out Cisse & Flamini |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2008/france/7406981.stm |publisher=BBC |date=28 May 2008 |access-date=9 June 2008 }}</ref> He played in the [[2008 FA Community Shield|2008 Community Shield]] against Manchester United, missing in the penalty shootout, which was won by United. On 18 September 2008, he scored Pompey's first-ever goal in [[UEFA Europa League|a major European competition]] against [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Portsmouth 2–0 Guimaraes Match Report |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7615243.stm |publisher=BBC |date=18 September 2008 |access-date=16 April 2010 |first=Ian |last=Hughes}}</ref> his third and final goal for the club. The first [[Misconduct (association football)#Red card|red card]] of Diarra's Premier League career came on 28 September 2008 when he was booked twice against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] at Fratton Park.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7626939.stm|title=Portsmouth 2-0 Tottenham|date=28 September 2008|work=BBC}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
[[File:Lass Messi.jpg|thumb|230px|Diarra against [[Lionel Messi]] during [[El Clásico]] at [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]], December 2011]]

On 17 December 2008, Portsmouth agreed a fee with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] for the transfer of Diarra on 1 January 2009 for a fee of around €20&nbsp;million (£18.88&nbsp;million), subject to a medical.<ref name=PortsmouthAcceptBid>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7787323.stm |title=Real Madrid unveil new boy Diarra |date=22 December 2008 |access-date=4 January 2018 |publisher=BBC }}</ref> He was assigned the number 6 shirt of [[Mahamadou Diarra]] for domestic competitions, as the Malian midfielder was out with a season-ending injury and the vacant number 39 for the Champions League. He wore the name "Lass" on the back of his shirt to avoid confusion with Mahamadou. Lassana Diarra's transfer was officially completed on 1 January 2009, the opening of the transfer window. Madrid had planned to add both Diarra and fellow new signing [[Klaas-Jan Huntelaar]] to their [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League|2008–09 Champions League]] squad, but both players had already featured in the same season's [[2008–09 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]] for previous clubs Portsmouth and [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] respectively; [[UEFA]] rules would allow only one of the pair to be registered<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.archive.uefa.com/uefa/keytopics/kind=512/newsid=791338.html |title=UEFA decision on Real Madrid |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=8 January 2009 |access-date=4 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113083604/http://en.archive.uefa.com/uefa/keytopics/kind%3D512/newsid%3D791338.html |archive-date=13 January 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.archive.uefa.com/uefa/keytopics/kind=512/newsid=792454.html |title=UEFA appeals body decision on Real Madrid |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=13 January 2009 |access-date=4 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113083604/http://en.archive.uefa.com/uefa/keytopics/kind%3D512/newsid%3D792454.html |archive-date=13 January 2016 }}</ref> by 1 February 2009, and eventually Diarra was selected to play in the competition.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202761186541/noticia/Noticia/Definitive_Champions_League_list.htm | title=Definitive Champions League list | publisher=Realmadrid.com | date=2 February 2009 | access-date=2 February 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090206080704/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202761186541/noticia/Noticia/Definitive_Champions_League_list.htm | archive-date=6 February 2009}}</ref>

Diarra's performance for Real Madrid in his first few months earned him a spot among the starting eleven on UEFA's 2008–09 La Liga Breakthrough Team. The Madridista joined Sevilla's [[Diego Perotti]] as the only foreigner on the list. According to the UEFA website, he "joined Real Madrid in the winter transfer window with a very low profile, although in a few short months he managed to convince the demanding Madridista fan base."

For the [[2009–10 in Spanish football|2009–10 season]] he was assigned the number 10 shirt after [[Wesley Sneijder]] moved to [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] and Mahamadou Diarra came back from injury and reclaimed the number 6 shirt. Lassana Diarra scored his first official goal for Madrid in the [[2009–10 La Liga]] opener against [[Deportivo de La Coruña]], providing his side with their winning goal in a 3–2 victory.

Manager José Mourinho included Diarra in his starting lineup for the first game of the [[2010–11 La Liga]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202817745826/1330013192288/noticia/Cronica/The_Whites_draw_in_league_debut_despite_having_several_chances_on_goal.htm |title=Real Madrid C.F. – Official Web Site – The Whites draw in league debut despite having several chances on goal |publisher=Realmadrid.com |date=29 August 2010 |access-date=28 April 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100903122055/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202817745826/1330013192288/noticia/Cronica/The_Whites_draw_in_league_debut_despite_having_several_chances_on_goal.htm |archive-date=3 September 2010}}</ref> Because Madrid bought [[Sami Khedira]], Diarra faced further competition to get into the squad. However, Mourinho said he would not be leaving and said that he saw Diarra as a starter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnstar.com/football/primera-liga/news/detail/item559312/Mourinho:-United-can-forget-Diarra/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120907103552/http://www.espnstar.com/football/primera-liga/news/detail/item559312/Mourinho:-United-can-forget-Diarra/ |archive-date=7 September 2012 |title=Football, La Liga, Mourinho: United can forget Diarra |publisher=Espnstar.Com |date=8 January 2011 |access-date=28 April 2011 |url-status=usurped}}</ref>

[[File:Ozil, di Maria and Diarra.jpg|thumb|left|190px|Diarra in 2012 alongside [[Mesut Özil]] and [[Ángel Di María]].]]

After speculation of Diarra leaving Real Madrid during the summer 2011 transfer window, during which he did not participate in the team's pre-season,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2011/07/09/2567799/real-madrids-lassana-diarra-left-out-of-pre-season-tour-of |title=Real Madrid's Lassana Diarra left out of pre-season tour of the United States - report |website=Goal.com |access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> Diarra finally stayed at the club, wearing the number 24 jersey after Sami Khedira had taken number 6 and [[Mesut Özil]] number 10 during the summer.

Diarra had a decent [[2011–12 Real Madrid CF season|2011–12 season]], culminating in winning the [[La Liga]] title with the club. He participated in the team's 2012 pre-season, and won the [[2012 Supercopa de España|2012]] [[Supercopa de España|Supercopa]] with the club. It seems he was forced out of the club alongside fellow midfield enforcer [[Esteban Granero]] to accommodate the stay of [[Kaká]], despite the latter being linked with an exit.

===Anzhi Makhachkala===
[[File:Lassana Diarra 2012.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Diarra with Anzhi in 2012]]

After falling down in the pecking order, Diarra was linked to join Russian side [[FC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Lass Diarra has Spartak offer – agent|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1115863/real-madrid%27s-lassana-diarra-has-spartak-moscow-offer---agent-?cc=5739=|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140829211336/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1115863/real-madrid's-lassana-diarra-has-spartak-moscow-offer---agent-?cc=5739=|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 August 2014|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=25 June 2012|access-date=11 September 2012}}</ref> On transfer deadline day, 31 August 2012, Diarra joined [[FC Anzhi Makhachkala|Anzhi Makhachkala]] on a four-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news|title=Official: Lassana Diarra joins Anzhi on four-year deal|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/69/transfer-zone/2012/09/03/3351869/official-lassana-diarra-joins-anzhi-on-four-year-deal|publisher=Goal.com|date=3 September 2012|access-date=11 September 2012}}</ref> He was originally meant to join merely on loan,<ref>{{cite news|title=Anzhi signs Lassana Diarra on loan from Real Madrid|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/69/transfer-zone/2012/09/01/3346275/anzhi-signs-lassana-diarra-on-loan-from-real-madrid|publisher=Goal.com|date=1 September 2012|access-date=11 September 2012}}</ref> but the club decided to make the deal permanent. After joining Anzhi, Diarra made an explanation about why he joined the club, claiming that [[Samuel Eto'o]] persuaded him to join and insisted money was not the reason he joined.<ref>{{cite news|title=Diarra: I joined Anzhi because of Eto'o, not the money|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2885/europe/2012/09/11/3367976/diarra-i-joined-anzhi-because-of-etoo-not-the-money|publisher=Goal.com|date=11 September 2012|access-date=11 September 2012}}</ref>

===Lokomotiv Moscow===
After Anzhi made their whole squad available for transfer due to cost-cutting, there was talk of a number of clubs interested in Diarra's services; [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] and [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] were thought to be interested in taking him back to France. However, he eventually signed a four-year contract with [[FC Lokomotiv Moscow|Lokomotiv Moscow]] on 20 August 2013, taking the number 85 shirt. He became the second most expensive transfer in Lokomotiv's history behind only [[Mbark Boussoufa]], who was signed by the club from	[[Anzhi Makhachkala]] in the summer of 2013 for €15m. Despite being sent off twice in his first matches for his new club against [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] and [[FC Tom Tomsk|Tom Tomsk]] respectively, Diarra quickly established himself in starting eleven, claiming one of two usual holding midfielder's posts alongside [[Dmitri Tarasov (footballer)|Dmitri Tarasov]]. In his first months at Lokomotiv, Diarra provided so many solid performances that someone even claimed that he was the strongest player in the history of the [[Russian Football Premier League|Russian Premier League]]. His growing influence in the team became acknowledged: in November and December 2013, he topped the monthly poll among Lokomotiv fans in social networks and received the Player of the Month award twice in a row. After the winter break, Diarra played only five out of eleven matches and his performances were a lot below the usual level.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]]|url=http://www.fclm.ru/ru/info/news/index.php?id_4=22683|script-title=ru:Ласс Диарра – игрок ноября!|language=ru|date=3 December 2013|access-date=3 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131207232917/http://www.fclm.ru/ru/info/news/index.php?id_4=22683|archive-date=7 December 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]]|url=http://www.fclm.ru/ru/info/news/index.php?id_4=22791|script-title=ru:Ласс Диарра – игрок декабря!|language=ru|date=16 December 2013|access-date=16 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216112831/http://www.fclm.ru/ru/info/news/index.php?id_4=22791|archive-date=16 December 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|publisher=Russian Football News|url=http://russianfootballnews.com/the-never-ending-story-about-lokomotiv-and-lassana-diarra|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531152137/http://russianfootballnews.com/the-never-ending-story-about-lokomotiv-and-lassana-diarra/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=31 May 2016|title=The Never Ending Story About Lokomotiv and Lassana Diarra|date=31 May 2016}}</ref>

Things turned sour for Diarra at Lokomotiv in the summer of 2014, when he fell out with head coach [[Leonid Kuchuk]]. The club alleged that Diarra then refused to participate in training.<ref name="BBC EU_law">{{Cite news |title=Lassana Diarra: Fifa transfer rules break EU law - top court rules |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cjwdydnl3w0o |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250723112122/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cjwdydnl3w0o |archive-date=2025-07-23 |access-date=2026-05-18 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2015-02-12 |title=West Ham's deal for Lassana Diarra falls through |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2015/0212/679602-west-hams-deal-for-lassana-diarra-falls-through/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240531191619/https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2015/0212/679602-west-hams-deal-for-lassana-diarra-falls-through/ |archive-date=2024-05-31 |access-date=2026-05-18 |work=RTE.ie |language=en}}</ref> Diarra claimed that Lokomotiv wanted to reduce his salary and tried to force him to accept a pay cut.<ref name="Le_Figaro Diarra">{{cite web|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/transferts/actualites/interdit-de-jouer-au-foot-lassana-diarra-tacle-la-fifa-737254|title=Interdit de jouer au foot, Lassana Diarra tacle la FIFA|language=fr|work=Le Figaro|date= 14 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210613045518/https://www.lefigaro.fr/sports/football/transferts/actualites/interdit-de-jouer-au-foot-lassana-diarra-tacle-la-fifa-737254|archive-date=2021-06-13|url-status=live}}</ref> In August 2014, Lokomotiv terminated Diarra's employment at the club for breach of contract on the grounds that he had refused to show up for training. At the time, his contract still had three years left before expiring in 2017.<ref name="BBC EU_law" /> The club then sought damages from Diarra for the breach of contract at [[FIFA]]'s Dispute and Resolution Chamber (DRC), who found in favour of Lokomotiv and determined that the player owed €10.5 million to his former club.<ref name="White_Case incompatible">{{Cite web |title=ECJ decision in the Diarra case: some of FIFA’s players transfer rules are incompatible with EU law {{!}} White & Case LLP |url=https://www.whitecase.com/insight-alert/ecj-decision-diarra-case-some-fifas-players-transfer-rules-are-incompatible-eu-law |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241107140155/https://www.whitecase.com/insight-alert/ecj-decision-diarra-case-some-fifas-players-transfer-rules-are-incompatible-eu-law |archive-date=2024-11-07 |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=www.whitecase.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Guardian Diarra_case">{{Cite news |date=2024-10-03 |title=The Lassana Diarra case: what is it and will it change football like Bosman? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/oct/03/lassana-diarra-case-explained-fifa-european-football |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241003132626/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/oct/03/lassana-diarra-case-explained-fifa-european-football |archive-date=2024-10-03 |access-date=2026-05-18 |work=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref> This ruling effectively banned Diarra from playing professionally for another club as long as his contractual dispute with Lokomotiv was not settled.<ref name="Guardian seeking">{{Cite news |date=2025-08-18 |title=Lassana Diarra seeking £56m from Fifa in compensation for past transfer rules |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/aug/18/lassana-diarra-seeking-56m-from-fifa-in-compensation-for-past-transfer-rules |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250822020411/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/aug/18/lassana-diarra-seeking-56m-from-fifa-in-compensation-for-past-transfer-rules |archive-date=2025-08-22 |access-date=2026-05-18 |work=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Le_Figaro Diarra" /> Kuchuk was sacked as head coach by the club in September 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-russia-lokomotiv/struggling-lokomotiv-moscow-sack-coach-kuchuk-idUKKBN0HD10G20140918|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200714043407/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-russia-lokomotiv/struggling-lokomotiv-moscow-sack-coach-kuchuk-idUKKBN0HD10G20140918|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 14, 2020|title=Struggling Lokomotiv Moscow sack coach Kuchuk|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=18 September 2014|access-date=10 July 2020|url-access=limited}}</ref>

===Aborted transfers and legal issues===
After Diarra left Lokomotiv Moscow, there were several months of speculation linking him with numerous European football clubs in 2014, including [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] and [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=31 October 2014 |title=Lassana Diarra flies in for Celtic talks, bid hits late stumbling block |url=https://www.the42.ie/lassana-diarra-in-celtic-talks-stumbling-block-1756022-Oct2014/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150717213632/https://www.the42.ie/lassana-diarra-in-celtic-talks-stumbling-block-1756022-Oct2014/ |archive-date=2015-07-17 |access-date=2026-05-19 |work=The42 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Celtic deny reports of Lassana Diarra deal|url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/latest/celtic-deny-reports-of-lassana-diarra-deal-1-3592588|publisher=The Scotsman|access-date=3 November 2014|date=3 November 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230924081819/https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/celtic/latest-celtic-news/celtic-deny-reports-of-lassana-diarra-deal-2474770|archive-date=2023-09-24}}</ref> He reached contract agreements with [[Inter Milan]] and [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in February 2015 but both moves were blocked by FIFA transfer regulations.<ref name="Le_Figaro Diarra" /><ref name="BBC West_Ham">{{Cite news |title=West Ham move for Diarra blocked |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/31356095 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029063107/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/31356095 |archive-date=2020-10-29 |access-date=2026-05-18 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB|date=11 February 2015}}</ref>

Belgian club [[Royal Charleroi S.C.|Sporting Charleroi]] made a conditional offer to Diarra on the proviso that the player could be registered in the Belgian league without Charleroi being made liable for any costs to Lokomotiv.<ref name="Guardian Diarra_case" /> The [[Royal Belgian Football Association|Belgian FA]] were unable to provide these assurances and, after FIFA refused to issue an International Transfer Certificate (ITC), Charleroi withdrew their offer on 19 February 2015.<ref name="BBC EU_law" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-09-29 |title=Will the Lassana Diarra case bring down transfer market as we know it? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/sep/29/will-the-lassana-diarra-case-bring-down-transfer-market-as-we-know-it |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241120021748/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/sep/29/will-the-lassana-diarra-case-bring-down-transfer-market-as-we-know-it |archive-date=2024-11-20 |access-date=2026-05-19 |work=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref> The club's concerns around the transfer related to a paragraph in FIFA's transfer regulations which stated that if a player breaches his contract, and the contract is subsequently terminated by the club, the player's new team is jointly liable to pay compensation to his previous club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Lassana Diarra judgement explained: What does it mean for footballers? |url=https://www.fifpro.org/en/articles/2025/05/the-lassana-diarra-judgement-explained-what-does-it-mean-for-footballers |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260218230422/https://www.fifpro.org/en/articles/2025/05/the-lassana-diarra-judgement-explained-what-does-it-mean-for-footballers |archive-date=2026-02-18 |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=www.fifpro.org |language=en-GB|date=2025-05-22|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-01-31 |title=Transfer rules back in the spotlight after Lassana Diarra case |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/football/transfer-rules-back-in-the-spotlight-after-lassana-diarra-case_sto6043459/story.shtml |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=www.tntsports.co.uk}}</ref><ref name="White_Case incompatible" />

In December 2015, Diarra took legal action against FIFA and the Belgian FA, challenging FIFA's transfer rules on the grounds that they violated his right to [[Freedom of movement for workers in the European Union|free movement within the EU]], which allows workers to seek employment in other member states without restrictions.<ref name="Guardian Diarra_case" /><ref name="White_Case incompatible" />

On 27 May 2016, the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] (CAS) upheld the decision by FIFA's DRC and Diarra was ordered to pay a 10 million euro fine to Lokomotiv Moscow for breach of contract, along with €110,000 to the CAS. He was also given a 15-month suspension from playing professional football and a suspension of payment of salary, both of which he had already served.<ref name="BBC EU_law" /><ref name="Goal ordered">{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3274/ligue-1/2016/05/28/24017022/lassana-diarra-ordered-to-pay-10-million-to-lokomotiv-moscow|title=Lassana Diarra ordered to pay €10 million to Lokomotiv Moscow|publisher=goal.com|date= 28 May 2016|last=Davie|first=Chris|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161106035314/http://m.goal.com/s/en-gb/news/3274/ligue-1/2016/05/28/24017022/lassana-diarra-ordered-to-pay-10-million-to-lokomotiv-moscow|archive-date=2016-11-06|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2017, a court in Charleroi ruled in Diarra's favour after deciding that FIFA and the Belgian FA had infringed upon EU law regarding the freedom of movement.<ref name="ESPN court_case">{{Cite news |title=Diarra to be paid €6m by FIFA, Belgian FA |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37511013/lassana-diarra-paid-6m-fifa-belgian-fa-winning-court-case |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602025719/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37511013/lassana-diarra-paid-6m-fifa-belgian-fa-winning-court-case |archive-date=2023-06-02 |access-date=2026-05-19 |work=ESPN.com |language=en|url-status=live|last=Holyman|first=Ian|date=2017-01-20}}</ref>

In a [[preliminary ruling]] of 4 October 2024, the [[Court of Justice of the European Union]] ruled in favour of Diarra, determining that FIFA's player contract rules violated European Union law.<ref>{{CELEX|62022CJ0650|text=Arrêt de la Cour (deuxième chambre) du 4 octobre 2024. Fédération internationale de football association (FIFA) contre BZ.}}, {{ECLI|ECLI:EU:C:2024:824}}, (Diarra [[Pseudonymization|pseudonymized]] as "BZ"), {{in lang|fr}}</ref><ref name="White_Case incompatible" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lawteacher.net/cases/diarra-fifa-case-3729.php?vref=1|title=Diarra v FIFA - Lassana Diarra Case|date=4 October 2024|access-date=5 October 2024|at=[https://www.lawteacher.net/ LawTeacher]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=MacInnes|first=Paul|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/oct/04/lassana-diarra-fifa-verdict-landmark-day-alter-balance-of-power-analysis|title=Diarra verdict a landmark day which could alter balance of football power|work=The Guardian |date=4 October 2024|access-date=5 October 2024|at=[https://www.theguardian.com/ The Guardian]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.goal.com/en-sa/lists/chelsea-real-madrid-star-lassana-diarra-court-case-against-fifa/blta27a1a9d32e49f60#csbb19ed47565c4565 |title=Ex-Chelsea & Real Madrid midfielder Lassana Diarra wins court case against FIFA in ruling that challenges player contract rules |publisher=Goal.com |date=4 October 2024 |access-date=5 October 2024}}</ref> As of October 2024, the main case is still pending at the [[:fr:Cour d'appel de Mons|Cour d'appel de Mons]] in Belgium.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} In December 2024, FIFA drafted interim amendments to the organisation's transfer regulations, accepting that they could be open to immediate challenge as a result of the court's decision.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Lassana Diarra: Fifa adapts transfer regulations after ruling over former France international |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ckgz9524l24o |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241223163144/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ckgz9524l24o |archive-date=2024-12-23 |access-date=2026-05-19 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In August 2025, Diarra restarted legal proceedings against FIFA and the Belgian FA after neither body approached him to discuss a settlement.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Fifa: Lassana Diarra seeks £56m in compensation in legal action |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c0r74y0jv9lo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250819232835/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c0r74y0jv9lo |archive-date=2025-08-19 |access-date=2026-05-19 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Marseille===
After serving a 15-month ban from football, Diarra signed for French [[Ligue 1]] side [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] on 24 July 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=Former Chelsea, Real Madrid player Lassana Diarra signs with Marseille|url=http://www.espnfc.com/marseille/story/2535451/lassana-diarra-signs-marseille-ligue-1-after-year-out|access-date=24 July 2015|date=24 July 2015|work=ESPNFC|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027000846/https://www.espn.com/soccer/marseille/story/2535451/lassana-diarra-signs-marseille-ligue-|archive-date=2020-10-27|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Lassana Diarra Olympian |url=https://www.om.net/node/184171 |publisher=Olympique de Marseille |date=24 July 2015 |access-date=24 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150808032528/https://www.om.net/node/184171 |archive-date=8 August 2015 |url-status=dead |language=Fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lawrence |first=Amy |date=2015-10-07 |title=From exile to Euro 2016? How Lassana Diarra came back from the brink |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/oct/07/lassana-diarra-exile-france-squad-euro-2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015203947/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/oct/07/lassana-diarra-exile-france-squad-euro-2016 |archive-date=2015-10-15 |access-date=2026-05-19 |work=the Guardian}}</ref> He made his debut for Marseille on 23 August and scored his first goal in a 6–0 victory over [[Troyes AC|Troyes]], while also achieving a 100 percent pass completion.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Scott|first1=A|title=Michel's Marseille Hit Troyes for Six|url=http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/michel-s-marseille-hit-troyes-for-six.htm|publisher=[[Ligue 1]]|access-date=27 August 2015|date=23 August 2015}}</ref> At the end of the [[2015–16 Ligue 1|2015–16]] season, he was named in the Ligue 1 Team of the Season by the [[National Union of Professional Footballers|UNFP]].<ref name="Team of the Year">{{cite news|url=https://frenchfootballdaily.com/2016/05/ligue-1-team-of-the-year-2016-unfp-team-of-the-season-201516/|title=Ligue 1 Team of the Year 2016- UNFP Team of the Season 2015/16|date=8 May 2016|work=French Football Daily}}</ref>

On 11 August 2016, Diarra was named as the club's new captain, replacing [[Steve Mandanda]] who had earlier joined [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.om.net/actualites/259611/lassana-diarra-nomme-capitaine-de-lom|title=Lassana Diarra named OM captain|website=Olympique de Marseille|date=11 August 2016|access-date=11 August 2016|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828084642/https://www.om.net/actualites/259611/lassana-diarra-nomme-capitaine-de-lom|archive-date=28 August 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Following [[Rudi Garcia]]'s appointment as new Marseille manager in October, however, Diarra's commitment to the club was questioned and he was later stripped of his captaincy in favour of loanee, [[Bafétimbi Gomis]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2016/bafetimbi-gomis-awarded-the-marseille-captaincy/|title=Bafétimbi Gomis awarded the Marseille captaincy|website=Get Football News France|date=20 November 2016|access-date=25 November 2016}}</ref> Having made only 11 league appearances for the season, Diarra was released by Marseille on 14 February 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espnfc.com/story/3060885/lassana-diarra-becomes-free-agent-after-marseille-contract-terminated|title=Lassana Diarra becomes free agent after Marseille contract terminated|website=ESPN|date=14 February 2017|access-date=27 February 2017}}</ref> Former manager [[José Anigo]] later claimed that the breakdown of relationship between club and player stemmed from then-chairman Vincent Labrune's failure to honour contractual promises to Diarra.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://le10sport.com/football/mercato/mercato-om-les-regrets-de-jose-anigo-concernant-lassana-diarra-315847|title=Mercato - OM : Les regrets de José Anigo concernant Lassana Diarra!|website=le 10 Sport|date=8 June 2017|access-date=15 June 2017|language=fr}}</ref>

===Al Jazira===
On 19 April 2017, Diarra joined Emirati club [[Al Jazira Club|Al Jazira]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eremnews.com/sports/football/arab/uae/806989 |script-title=ar:لاسانا ديارا إلى الجزيرة الإماراتي |language=ar |work=إرم نيوز |last1=الله |first1=محمد عطا |access-date=28 April 2017 |archive-date=24 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170424025022/http://www.eremnews.com/sports/football/arab/uae/806989 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made five appearances in the [[2017–18 UAE Pro-League|UAE Pro-League]] before mutually terminating his contract with the club on 24 December 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/soccer-transfers/story/3324180/lassana-diarra-becomes-free-agent-after-al-jazira-contract-terminated|title=Lassana Diarra becomes free agent after Al Jazira contract terminated|website=ESPN|date=24 December 2017}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
On 23 January 2018, Diarra joined [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] on a one-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.psg.fr/pro/article/lassana-diarra-au-paris-saint-germain|title=Lassana Diarra au Paris Saint-Germain|website=psg.fr|date=23 January 2018|access-date=23 January 2018|archive-date=22 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181022073441/https://www.psg.fr/pro/article/lassana-diarra-au-paris-saint-germain|url-status=dead}}</ref> The France international has become the 436th player to represent the capital club.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://en.psg.fr/pro/article/lassana-diarra-makes-debut|title=Lassana Diarra makes debut - PSG.fr|website=en.psg.fr|language=en|access-date=31 January 2018|archive-date=31 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131200641/https://en.psg.fr/pro/article/lassana-diarra-makes-debut|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut for the club under coach [[Unai Emery]] on 30 January 2018 in the 3–2 [[Coupe de la Ligue]] semi-final win against [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Stade Rennais]]<ref name=":0" /> On 21 February 2019, Diarra and PSG mutually terminated his contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://m.leparisien.fr/sports/football/psg/lassana-diarra-a-resilie-son-contrat-avec-paris-19-02-2019-8015478.php|access-date=19 February 2019|title=Lassana Diarra a résilié son contrat avec Paris|date=19 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47319557|title=Paris St-Germain: Lassana Diarra contract terminated|date=21 February 2019|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref> He subsequently announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.90min.com/posts/6302384-lassana-diarra-announces-retirement-from-football-after-being-released-by-paris-saint-germain|title=Lassana Diarra Announces Retirement From Football After Being Released by Paris Saint-Germain|publisher=90 Min|date=21 February 2019|access-date=1 April 2019|archive-date=1 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401141931/https://www.90min.com/posts/6302384-lassana-diarra-announces-retirement-from-football-after-being-released-by-paris-saint-germain|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==International career==

===Youth team===
Diarra won 18 caps for the [[France national under-21 football team|France under-21s]]. Perhaps his most notable performance came in the [[2006 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification play-offs]] second-leg match against [[England national under-21 football team|England]] at the [[Stade Marcel Picot]] in November 2005. With the match several minutes from full-time and seemingly destined for extra time (the aggregate score was 2–2), he received the ball in the England penalty box, where a challenge from [[Kieran Richardson]] brought Diarra down. A penalty was given for the foul, and Diarra's teammate [[Jimmy Briand]] scored the penalty, shooting the ball past [[Scott Carson]]. France won the tie 3–2 on aggregate and thus qualified for the finals to be held in [[Portugal]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ambrose strike saves England |url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0de690507364-703629779693-1000--ambrose-strike-saves-england/|publisher=UEFA |date=11 November 2005 |access-date=5 February 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=England undone by brave Briand |url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0de691268380-e7cf2813bc62-1000--england-undone-by-brave-briand/|publisher=UEFA |date=15 December 2005 |access-date=5 February 2014 }}</ref>

===Senior team===
Diarra was selected for the [[French national football team|senior team]] by coach [[Raymond Domenech]] for a [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|UEFA Euro 2008 qualifier]] away to [[Lithuania national football team|Lithuania]] on 24 March 2007. He started the match, alongside Claude Makélélé and [[Jérémy Toulalan]] in midfield, and played the full 90 minutes.<ref>{{cite news |title=Anelka to the rescue for France |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b89f95103-63eceb0e8218-1000--anelka-to-the-rescue-for-france/ |publisher=UEFA |date=24 March 2007 |access-date=5 February 2014 }}</ref> He was also selected that year for a [[Exhibition game|friendly match]] against [[Austria national football team|Austria]] on 28 March 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/997342 |title=DIARRA RECEIVES FRANCE CALL &#124; News Article &#124; News &#124; Official Site &#124; Chelsea Football Club |website=www.chelseafc.com |access-date=2 February 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140205102026/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/997342 |archive-date=5 February 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Diarra's consistent club performances in 2008 resulted in him being picked for the France squad for [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]], ahead of high-calibre players such as [[Djibril Cissé]] and Mathieu Flamini.<ref name="France leave out Cisse & Flamini"/> France was eliminated in the group stage of Euro 2008 and Diarra did not feature in any of his country's three group stage matches.<ref>{{cite news |title=Romania 0–0 France Match Report|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2008/7363325.stm |publisher=BBC |date=9 June 2008 |access-date=21 June 2008 |first=Chris |last=Whyatt}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Netherlands 4–1 France Match Report|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2008/7363369.stm |publisher=BBC |date=13 June 2008 |access-date=21 June 2008 |first=Phil |last=McNulty}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=France 0–2 Italy & Netherlands 2–0 Romania Match Reports|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2008/7363384.stm |publisher=BBC |date=17 June 2008 |access-date=21 June 2008 |first=Phil |last=McNulty}}</ref>

Following the international retirement of fellow defensive midfielder Claude Makélélé, Diarra was called up for Domenech's France squad in the 20 August 2008 friendly with [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Les Blues omit Nasri|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11800_3970921,00.html |publisher=Sky Sports |date=12 August 2008 |access-date=12 August 2008 }}</ref> By the end of the 2010 World Cup qualifying campaign, Diarra had made 26 appearances for France.<ref name="FFF">{{cite web |url=http://www.fff.fr/equipes-de-france/tous-les-joueurs/fiche-joueur/329-lassana-diarra |title=Lassana |publisher=Fff.fr |date=29 January 2009 |access-date=5 February 2014 |archive-date=29 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929054140/https://www.fff.fr/equipes-de-france/tous-les-joueurs/fiche-joueur/329-lassana-diarra |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 11 May 2010, Diarra was named to the preliminary squad of Domenech's squad to play in the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]]. He was later named to the shortened list of players and was expected to be a starter alongside Jérémy Toulalan in the midfield. On 22 May, however, while training with the national team in the high-altitude commune of [[Tignes]], it was announced that Diarra was dropping out of the squad due to his suffering severe intestinal pain and stomach cramps as a result of the altitude. A follow-up medical check revealed that Diarra would require rest for an indefinite period.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lassana Diarra forfait |url=https://www.algerie360.com/lassana-diarra-forfait/ |publisher=Algerie |date=22 May 2010 |access-date=5 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215631/http://www.algerie360.com/sport/football/lassana-diarra-forfait/ |archive-date=3 March 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref> His club, Real Madrid, later revealed that Diarra was resting at home following medical advice due to asthenic syndrome secondary to [[sickle-cell anemia]], a genetic blood disorder characterized by red blood cells that assume an abnormal, rigid, sickle shape.<ref>{{cite news |title=Diarra resting after missing out on World Cup |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/soccer/2010-05-23-2541772632_x.htm |work=USA Today |date=23 May 2010 |access-date=24 May 2010 |first=Jerome |last=Pugmire}}</ref>

After an absence of over five years, Diarra received a surprise recall to the French team following a fine run of form at the beginning of the [[2015–16 Ligue 1|2015–16 season]]. Upon announcing his return to the squad, France manager [[Didier Deschamps]] highlighted Diarra's performances in a struggling Marseille side as the reason behind his inclusion.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37436474/lassana-diarra-returns-france-squad-five-years|title=Lassana Diarra makes return to France squad after five-year absence
|date=1 October 2015|access-date=9 May 2025|work=[[ESPN]]|last=Rodden|first=Mark}}</ref>

On 12 May 2016, Diarra was named in the [[France national football team|France]] squad for [[UEFA Euro 2016]]. On 30 May 2016, he played the first half of the friendly match against [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]] and was replaced at half-time by [[N'Golo Kanté]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espnfc.com.au/france/story/2870292/ngolo-kante-in-france-squad-for-euro-2016-but-hatem-ben-arfa-and-alexandre-lacazette-out|title=N'Golo Kante in France's Euros squad; Lacazette, Gameiro, Ben Arfa miss out|date=12 May 2016|work=ESPN}}</ref> However, Diarra later was forced to pull out of the squad because of a swelling in his left knee. He was replaced by [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]'s [[Morgan Schneiderlin]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36422929|title=Euro 2016: Lassana Diarra ruled out, Morgan Schneiderlin comes in|date=31 May 2016|work=BBC}}</ref>

==Playing style==
Despite being an aggressive, hard-tackling and hard-working player, Diarra has unusually good ball control for a defensive midfielder, and has been praised for his physical strength in defence, as well as his composure, and strong mentality.<ref name="five outstanding performers"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1193041476158/1202773333597/noticia/Noticia/A_pleasant_surprise.htm |title=Real Madrid C.F. – Official Web Site – A pleasant surprise |publisher=Realmadrid.com |date=4 June 2009 |access-date=28 April 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101231195159/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1193041476158/1202773333597/noticia/Noticia/A_pleasant_surprise.htm |archive-date=31 December 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/lassana-diarra-talentspotter|title=Lassana Diarra: Talentspotter|publisher=FourFourTwo|date=1 February 2006|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/3331251/Hard-working-Bolton-Wanderers-reap-the-rewards-against-Manchester-City-Football.html|title=Hard-working Bolton Wanderers reap the rewards against Manchester City|work=The Telegraph|author1=Henry Winter|date=2 November 2008|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/international/lassana-diarra-the-heartbreaking-story-of-the-france-international-defying-isis-a6736341.html|title=Lassana Diarra: The heartbreaking story of the France international defying Isis|work=The Independent|author1=Michael E. Miller|date=16 November 2015|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref> Although he is usually deployed in the [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|centre of midfield]] as a ball-winner, due to his energy, tenacity, and tackling abilities, he is also a creative player who can dictate the tempo of his team's play with his tidy and intelligent passing from [[Midfielder#Deep-lying playmaker (Strolling 10)|deep midfield positions]] after winning back possession; he is also capable of being an offensive threat due to his ability to get forward and score goals, courtesy of his striking ability from distance.<ref name="five outstanding performers">{{cite web|url=https://www.espnfc.us/french-ligue-1/9/blog/post/2735527/lassana-diarra-leads-five-outstanding-performers-of-ligue-1|title=Lassana Diarra leads five outstanding performers of the Ligue 1 season so far|publisher=ESPN FC|author1=Julien Laurens|date=1 December 2015|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="Arsenal take Diarra from Chelsea">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/arsenal/6973572.stm|title=Arsenal take Diarra from Chelsea|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 August 2007|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/france/11997612/England-vs-France-Lassana-Diarra-back-at-Wembley-after-comeback-tainted-by-tragedy-during-Paris-terrorist-attacks.html|title=England vs France: Lassana Diarra back at Wembley after comeback tainted by tragedy during Paris terrorist attacks|work=The Telegraph|author1=Ian Hawkey|date=15 November 2015|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref> Due to his many attributes and versatility, Madrid's [[La Sexta]] television commentators refer to him as a "''todocampista''," or "jack of all trades",<ref name="goal.com">{{cite web|author=Editorial |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1717/editorial/2009/11/24/1639776/el-clasico-inquisition-real-madrid-barcelonas-unsung-heroes |title=El Clasico Inquisition: Real Madrid & Barcelona's Unsung Heroes |publisher=Goal.com |date=24 November 2009 |access-date=28 April 2011}}</ref> and he has also occasionally played in more [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|advanced midfield]] roles, or as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|right back]].<ref name="Arsenal take Diarra from Chelsea"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hitc.com/en-gb/topic/lassana-diarra/|title=Lassana Diarra|publisher=HITC.com|access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref>

[[Jimmy Bullard]] said on facing Diarra: ‘he was a bit like [[N'Golo Kanté|Kanté]]. When you look at him you think “I can deal with that, he’s fine. He’s 5”2”, I reckon I can handle this”. Unbelievable. What a player he was.’<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-03 |title=You've done me' - What Jimmy Bullard said to Danny Murphy after being told to mark Pompey sensation Lassana Diarra |url=https://www.portsmouth.co.uk/sport/football/portsmouth-fc/youve-done-me-what-former-fulham-midfielder-jimmy-bullard-said-to-danny-murphy-after-being-told-to-mark-portsmouth-sensation-lassana-diarra-4168536 |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=The News |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Diarra is a practising Muslim. On 13 November 2015, his cousin Asta Diakité was killed during [[November 2015 Paris attacks|a series of coordinated terrorist attacks]] in [[Paris]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/actualite-france/2015/11/20/01016-20151120ARTFIG00232--pantin-on-pleure-asta-jeune-musulmane-tuee-par-les-terroristes.php |title=À Pantin, on pleure Asta, jeune musulmane tuée par les terroristes |first=Eugénie |last=Bastié |date=20 November 2015 |access-date=23 December 2019 |newspaper=[[Le Figaro]]|language=fr}}</ref> At the time, Diarra was playing for France in an international friendly against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] at the [[Stade de France]], just north of Paris in [[Saint-Denis, Seine-Saint-Denis|Saint-Denis]].<ref name="caughtoffside">{{cite news|url=http://www.caughtoffside.com/2015/11/14/cousin-of-ex-chelsea-arsenal-real-madrid-star-international-midfielder-killed-in-paris-attack|title= Cousin of ex-Chelsea, Arsenal, Real Madrid star & international midfielder killed in Paris attacks|last=Fulco|first=Hugo|date=14 November 2015|publisher=CaughtOffside|access-date=14 November 2015}}</ref>

Diarra grew up supporting [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].<ref name=Talentspotter />
